options.text: A group of parts that work together and depend on one another
Any large object made of metal
A single part doing one job by itself
A list of materials kept in one place

items.explanation: A system is a group of connected parts that work together toward a purpose. The parts depend on one another, which is what makes it a system instead of a collection.

items.stem: A pile of bicycle parts sits on the floor. When does it become a system?

options.text: As soon as all the parts are in the same room
Only when the parts are painted the same color
When the parts are connected so they work together
It is already a system while still in the pile

items.explanation: The parts become a system only when they are connected so they work together. A disconnected pile is just a collection.

items.stem: At a traffic intersection, the electricity and the cars arriving are best described as the system's

options.text: outputs
inputs
boundary
feedback

items.explanation: Inputs are what enter a system, such as energy, material, or information. Electricity and arriving cars enter the intersection, so they are inputs.

items.stem: Sensors report how many cars are waiting, and the controller uses that information to change the light timing. This returning information is an example of

options.text: a subsystem
an input
feedback
a boundary

items.explanation: Feedback is information about a system's output that is sent back to adjust how the system works. The sensor reports let the controller adjust the timing.

items.stem: A single traffic light is one part of the whole city transportation network. The single light is best described as a

options.text: boundary
subsystem
process
output

items.explanation: A subsystem is a smaller system that works as one part inside a larger system. The traffic light is a subsystem of the city transportation network.

items.stem: What is the main reason a change in one component can affect other components?

options.text: The components interact, so effects pass between them
Components always fail at the same time
Every component does the exact same job
Components have no connection to each other

items.explanation: Components interact, meaning one part affects another. Those interactions are the connections that let a change travel through the system.

items.stem: An engineer wants to study a city's traffic without tracking every single car. What tool is most useful?

options.text: A model that shows the parts and how they connect
A complete copy of every street and car
A photograph of one intersection
A list of every driver's name

items.explanation: A model is a simplified representation that keeps the important parts and interactions and leaves out the rest, which is exactly what the engineer needs.

items.stem: Which statement about models is correct?

options.text: A good model includes every detail of the real system
A model leaves out some details on purpose to focus on what matters
Models can only ever be physical objects
A model must look exactly like the real thing

items.explanation: Models are tools, not copies. A useful model leaves out details that do not matter so it can focus on the parts and interactions that do.

items.stem: The teeth of a zipper are arranged so they interlock and hold it closed. This shows that a system's

options.text: function has nothing to do with its parts
structure, or arrangement of parts, shapes what it can do
parts can be rearranged with no effect
boundary decides its color

items.explanation: Structure is the arrangement of parts, and it shapes function. Rearrange the same zipper teeth and the zipper can no longer do its job.

items.stem: Why does one broken traffic light cause problems throughout a whole city?

options.text: Traffic problems happen at random with no cause
The broken light affects only its own corner
The parts are connected, so the failure spreads along their interactions
Every light in the city breaks at the same moment

items.explanation: The city is a system of connected parts. The broken light backs up the next intersection, which backs up the next, so the failure travels along the interactions that connect the parts.
